title: Child and youth anthropometry for minimum-rider rules
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Children are over-represented in the incident review, and REQ-F2 needs minimum rider height and mass. CDC growth charts and NHANES give public reference data.
objective: Summarise height, mass, hip circumference and torso proxies for ages 6–17 from public sources, and map them against common ride height limits (e.g., 42, 48, 54 in.).
acceptanceCriteria: Public sources only, cited by table
Shows which ride height thresholds correspond to which body sizes
Makes no recommendation that children use RideBelt; it is input data for REQ-F2
